headline: Cross-cohort and cross-cell-line tests expose instability in siRNA and CRISPRi perturbation predictions
label: Reliability Audits For Biological Design
summary: New preprints pair siRNA potency models with external benchmarks and show CRISPRi rankings and knockdown transfer depend on cohort and cell-line context.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluating whether predictive models and screen-derived rankings hold outside the setting in which they were derived. TRACE reports that CRISPRi rejuvenation rankings change with the aging cohort and track proliferation programs. The Perturb-seq study finds knockdown responses transfer to new cell lines only when part of each line is screened, motivating the set-based CASTER adaptation. On the constructive side, Silscore uses positional nearest-neighbour thermodynamics with sparse identity terms and reports strong transfer to external data, while DeepRNAi predicts on- and off-target siRNA activity and releases a training and benchmark dataset. Together these emphasize external validation and benchmark release over in-distribution performance.
